notes: SUPERSEDED for training use by harness-bench-swe-rebench-openhands-pi-records-20261010-v3 (2026-10-10, the registered digest→view conversion; this corpus stays as published and the trainer refuses its digest parts). Harness-bench native records (natlang.teacher_training_turn.native/1, plans/neuralese/HARNESS_BENCH.md §2), supersedes harness-bench-swe-rebench-openhands-pi-records-20261010-v1. Built 2026-10-10 by harness_bench_build.sh at code commit b4543ebd: same surface.json and prepared.jsonl as v1 (copied, byte-identical), replay and records re-run with the fix that an OpenHands bash timeout notice ('[The command has no new output after N seconds. ... send keys ("C-c", "C-z", "C-d") ... or use the timeout parameter in execute_bash for future commands.]', or its 'timed out after N seconds' form) is a divergence point: pi's bash waits for the command, so pi would never show that notice; replay stops before that step and records keep only the verified prefix. 492 resolved trajectories prepared, 489 replayed (3 clone failures, NREL/hescore-hpxml), 305 fully verified and 184 verified up to their first divergence; 22,468 of 22,652 steps verified. Divergences: task_tracker 112, bash soft timeout (OpenHands-only interaction) 31, read text mismatch 22, read failed in pi 8, write failed for the teacher 5, read failed for the teacher 4, execute_bash interactive input 1, str_replace_editor other 1. 3,843 records (3,731 train / 112 test), 20,302 digest parts; no record contains the soft-timeout notice (v1: 6). Per-record admission is in each record (harness-bench-criteria/2: resolved, pi-replayed-verified, exact-mapping; all 3,843 pass). surface_sha256 is the sha256 of the sorted-key JSON of surface.json that every record's provenance carries; surface_file_sha256 is the file's bytes. Gold and test patches are not in any file. Corpus-level training admission is held: pending text-twin rendering with the fixed renderer and recipe cohort declaration (HARNESS_BENCH.md §7 step 2). Stored on /mnt/external with the other corpora (all files < 1 GiB; a finished, held corpus is not latency-critical).
